subject: Recap + next steps: NorthStar dedicated capacity qualification and canary plan
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Emily Ross <emily.ross@northstarhealth.com>, Carlos Mendez <carlos.m@northstarhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Recap: Dedicated capacity conversation this morning

Hi Emily / Carlos — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap from our side plus proposed next steps so we have alignment.

Call highlights (what you confirmed):
- Primary goal: move latency-sensitive clinical note generation to a private, dedicated pool to guarantee isolation and predictable per-request latency for patient-facing workflows.
- Current pain: intermittent 2–4x token-latency spikes during peak ingest, and audit concerns about multi-tenant caches.
- Desired SLA: sustained 99.95% availability, and p95 inference latency target of <= 450ms for typical 512-token calls.
- Isolation need: fully isolated VPC-backed Dedicated pool with customer KMS support and audit logs retained 2 years for compliance.
- Scaling profile: steady baseline of ~40 concurrent inference connections with burst to 120 for nightly batch jobs; peak tokens/day estimate ~120M.

Redwood preliminary qualification summary:
- Recommended starting footprint: 6x A100-equivalent GPUs in a private pool (can be mapped to our Dedicated offering). This supports steady concurrency with room for autoscaling bursts; we proposed a canary run to validate latency at scale.
- Config knobs to tune: continuous batching window, prefix/KV caching for repeated schemas, and quantization profile (FP16 -> 4-bit) for batch jobs where quality trade-off is acceptable.
- Compliance: we can provide SOC 2 summary and KMS/HSM integration steps; will include SOC artifacts in follow-up.

Immediate next steps (proposed owner):
1) Redwood to share a short technical config workbook (attached) and our canary runbook — Stephanie (ACTION: send today) [attachment: nsh-dedicated-config-v1.xlsx; canary-runbook.md]
2) NorthStar to confirm acceptance criteria for canary (SLA & p95 target) and a preferred 2-week window in Dec — Emily (ACTION: propose windows by Tue)
3) Procurement to confirm PO cadence and required contract terms; cc'd procurement email — Carlos/Dylan (ACTION: share procurement checklist)

Open questions from our side:
- Do you expect model updates (new weights) to be pushed weekly or monthly? This affects rollback/runbook for cache warming.
- Any on-prem data egress constraints we should be aware of (e.g., no plaintext logs outside VPC)?

Thanks — I’ll attach the workbook and runbook here and loop in Marissa for technical onboarding.

—
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132
Redwood Inference

Attachments: nsh-dedicated-config-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), canary-runbook.md (markdown)

From: Emily Ross <emily.ross@northstarhealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendez <carlos.m@northstarhealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Dedicated capacity conversation this morning

Thanks Stephanie — this is helpful and aligns with our thinking. A few clarifications from my side:

1) Model cadence: we expect to push model retrains monthly for the proprietary clinical summarization model, and smaller prompt/template updates weekly.
2) Logs: we cannot permit plaintext inference logs to leave our VPC; audit logs and aggregated telemetry are ok as long as they are encrypted with our KMS.
3) Canary acceptance criteria:
   - No more than 1.5x baseline p95 degradation during a simulated 4-hour peak test
   - No failed inferences above 0.2% during the run

We can do the canary window Dec 14–18 (preferred) or Dec 21–23 (backup). I’ll confirm with the infra team later today.

Also, please include SOC 2 evidence — we need at least the relevant control mapping and a PDF of the report for legal.

Best,
Emily
Emily Ross
Director, AI Platforms | NorthStar Health
emily.ross@northstarhealth.com

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Emily Ross <emily.ross@northstarhealth.com>, Carlos Mendez <carlos.m@northstarhealth.com>, procurement@northstarhealth.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T13:30:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up: config workbook + SOC2 + canary runbook

Hi Emily / Carlos / procurement team — attaching the requested artifacts and a short execution plan. Marissa is copied for the technical go/no-go on the canary; Dylan is copied for procurement coordination.

Attachments included:
- nsh-dedicated-config-v1.xlsx (recommended pool sizing, concurrency profiles, batch window settings)
- northstar-soc2-summary.pdf (control mapping + evidence index)
- canary-runbook.md (step-by-step: traffic generator profile, acceptance gates, rollback steps)

Key notes from the workbook (TL;DR):
- We modeled two options: "Baseline Reserved" (6 GPUs) and "Buffered Reserved" (8 GPUs + burst to shared). Baseline should meet the 40 concurrent baseline + bursts to 120 with modest autoscale latency; Buffered gives headroom for iterative retrains.
- We recommend starting with Baseline Reserved + a 2-week canary (Dec 14–18) using production traffic replay at 1.2x to validate cache warming and p95 targets.
- SLA proposal: 99.95% uptime SLA, with credits tied to rolling 30-day availability. For latency, we include p95 latency target in the SLO appendix and an operational escalation path.

Marissa — can you confirm the canary traffic profile in the runbook matches what we'd need to validate prefix/KV cache warm-up and autoscale behavior? Specific ask: simulate 120 concurrent connections, with 20% of calls being 1–2k token longer-form generation.

Dylan — for procurement: we expect a standard reserved capacity MSA + an order form. If you can share your procurement contact and required PO terms (net-30/45, PO recipient email, any required DPAs), we’ll assemble a quote and contract redlines.

Next tangible dates:
- Emily confirms canary window by 2026-12-01 (Emily)
- Redwood sends formal quote + draft order form by 2026-12-03 (Stephanie/Dylan)
- Technical kickoff for canary one week before the window (Marissa)

Thanks — reach out if you want a quick 20-min pre-canary tech sync.

—
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments: nsh-dedicated-config-v1.xlsx, northstar-soc2-summary.pdf, canary-runbook.md

From: Carlos Mendez <carlos.m@northstarhealth.com>

Date: 2026-11-29T15:43:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: config workbook + SOC2 + canary runbook

Stephanie / team — appreciate the fast turnaround and the detailed workbook. A couple quick procurement and ops items from my side:

- Procurement ask: please send a formal quote with line-item breakdown (reserved GPUs, support tier, data residency add-on) and a sample order form. Our legal needs to see the SLA appendix and the DPA.
- Ops ask: confirm whether the isolation is at the tenant level (full VPC isolation per customer) vs. per-model namespace. We need tenant-level isolation.
- Canary window confirmed: Dec 14–18 works for infra. Emily will send the exact daily time blocks; keep the runbook flexible to start at 02:00 local if needed.

If you can get the quote and SOC2 PDF to procurement@northstarhealth.com today, I’ll route it through our procurement queue.

Thanks,
Carlos
VP, Infrastructure | NorthStar Health
carlos.m@northstarhealth.com
